# 2 Kings Chapter 4 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 224v–226r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_004_page_001.jpg, 2KI_004_page_002.jpg, 2KI_004_page_003.jpg, 2KI_004_page_004.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now the wife of one of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. But the creditor has come to take my two children as his slaves."

**2** Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She said, "Your servant has nothing in the house except a flask of oil."

**3** He said, "Go, borrow vessels from all your neighbors — empty vessels. Do not get too few.

**4** Then go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all those vessels. Set each one aside as it fills."

**5** So she went from him and shut the door behind herself and her sons. They kept bringing vessels to her, and she kept pouring.

**6** When the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." He said, "There is not another." And the oil stopped.

**7** She came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debts, and you and your sons can live on the rest."

**8** One day Elisha went to Shunem, where a prominent woman lived. She urged him to eat a meal, and from then on, whenever he passed through, he would stop there to eat.

**9** She said to her husband, "I know that this is a holy man of God who is continually passing our way.

**10** Let us make a small room on the roof with walls, and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp, so that whenever he comes to us he can stay there."

**11** One day he came there and turned into the upper room and lay down.

**12** He said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." When he had called her, she stood before him.

**13** He said to Gehazi, "Say to her: 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Shall we speak on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I dwell among my own people."

**14** He said, "What then can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "She has no son, and her husband is old."

**15** He said, "Call her." When he had called her, she stood in the doorway.

**16** He said, "At this season, about this time next year, you shall embrace a son." She said, "No, my lord, O man of God — do not deceive your servant!"

**17** But the woman conceived and bore a son at that season, about the time Elisha had spoken to her.

**18** When the child had grown, he went out one day to his father among the reapers.

**19** He said to his father, "My head, my head!" His father said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."

**20** He carried him and brought him to his mother. The child sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.

**21** She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.

**22** She called to her husband and said, "Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, that I may hurry to the man of God and come back."

**23** He said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." She said, "All is well."

**24** She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive fast! Do not slow down for me unless I tell you."

**25** So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "There is the Shunammite.

**26** Run to meet her and say to her, 'Is all well with you? Is all well with your husband? Is all well with the child?'" She answered, "All is well."

**27** But when she came to the man of God at the mountain, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi came to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for she is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me."

**28** She said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"

**29** He said to Gehazi, "Tie up your garment and take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the face of the child."

**30** But the mother of the child said, "As the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he arose and followed her.

**31** Gehazi went on ahead and laid the staff on the face of the child, but there was no sound or response. He went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The child has not awakened."

**32** When Elisha came into the house, the child was lying dead on his bed.

**33** He went in and shut the door behind the two of them and prayed to the LORD.

**34** Then he went up and lay on the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. As he stretched himself upon him, the flesh of the child became warm.

**35** He got up and walked back and forth in the house, then went up and stretched himself upon him. The child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

**36** He called Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite." When she came to him, he said, "Pick up your son."

**37** She came and fell at his feet, bowing to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

**38** Elisha returned to Gilgal during the famine in the land. While the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Set on the large pot and cook stew for the sons of the prophets."

**39** One of them went out into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine. He gathered from it a lapful of wild gourds and came back and sliced them into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.

**40** They poured it out for the men to eat, but as they began eating, they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.

**41** He said, "Then bring flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

**42** A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God bread of the firstfruits — twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people, that they may eat."

**43** But his servant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" He said, "Give it to the people, that they may eat, for thus says the LORD: 'They shall eat and have some left over.'"

**44** So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

This chapter collects four Elisha miracle stories that demonstrate the breadth of prophetic power: economic liberation (oil), resurrection (the Shunammite's son), purification (poisoned stew), and multiplication (feeding the hundred). The Shunammite woman is the chapter's dominant character — unnamed but unforgettable, her independence, grief, and accusation ("Did I ask for a son?") make her one of the most fully human figures in Kings. The structural parallel with Elijah's miracles (1 Kgs 17) is systematic: oil miracle, son raised, food provided. Elisha does what Elijah did, confirming the double portion.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "sons of the prophets" vs. "prophets' guild"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "sons of the prophets"
- **PNEUMA:** "prophets' guild"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "sons of the prophets" — consistent with ch.2 ruling; the Hebrew idiom is preserved.

### V.8 — "great woman" / "wealthy woman" / "prominent woman"
- **EMET:** "a-great woman [ishah gedolah]"
- **LOGOS:** "a wealthy woman"
- **PNEUMA:** "a prominent woman"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a prominent woman" — *gedolah* means "great" in social standing, not exclusively wealthy. PNEUMA captures the breadth better than LOGOS's narrower "wealthy."

### V.13 — "I dwell among my own people" vs. "I live contentedly among my own people"
- **EMET:** "In-the-midst of-my-people I-am-dwelling"
- **LOGOS:** "I dwell among my own people"
- **PNEUMA:** "I have everything I need — I live contentedly among my own people"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I dwell among my own people" — the Hebrew is tersely understated. PNEUMA's expansion, while capturing the meaning, adds words not in the text.

### V.16 — "do not deceive" vs. "don't raise my hopes"
- **EMET:** "do-not deceive [al tekhazzev]"
- **LOGOS:** "do not deceive"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't raise my hopes like that"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "do not deceive" — *kazav* means to lie/deceive. PNEUMA's paraphrase is emotionally apt but loses the verb's accusatory force.

### V.40 — "death in the pot" vs. "poison in the pot"
- **EMET:** "Death in-the-pot [mavet ba-sir]"
- **LOGOS:** "there is death in the pot"
- **PNEUMA:** "there's poison in the pot"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "there is death in the pot" — the Hebrew says *mavet* (death), not poison. The dramatic exclamation should be preserved.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
